beats.trigger: ## Building Agent Systems
beats.got: nothing new, it is a title

beats.trigger: A system remembers, grows, and compounds. Chat doesn't.
beats.got: Something about a thing that keeps notes. I do not know what 'compounds' means for a depot.

beats.trigger: Karpathy's LLM Wiki post.
beats.got: A homework list. I did not do it. Confluence and OneDrive, I don't know if we have those connected.

beats.trigger: **See** the three layers (raw sources, memory, rules file) and why plain text
beats.got: Five things I will do. 'Memory' and 'rules file' are still just words.

beats.trigger: What's the difference between asking an LLM a question and having an LLM maintain a knowledge base for you?
beats.got: Long text in English. I understood: new folder, old stuff stays away. Question I cannot answer yet.

beats.trigger: what challenge are you carrying that isn't solved yet?
beats.got: This one I can answer: late deliveries and the weekly reporting. A real problem, not a slide.

beats.trigger: The schedule makes the agent run again without a fresh prompt and write the next result in the same place.
beats.got: It does the thing every morning by itself. That is closer to reporting than a chatbot.

beats.trigger: Ask the agent to interview you with three questions, one at a time, and write `./challenge.md`
beats.got: It asked me three short questions and wrote half a page about my dispatch load. It was about right. I fixed the depot names.

beats.trigger: Keep it narrow enough that 5–8 topic pages cover it.
beats.got: 45 minutes of work on one topic. Okay, I will try.

beats.trigger: If an email thread, deck, or doc feels sensitive, skip it.
beats.got: Be careful with customer data. Good, nobody will have a problem with that.

beats.trigger: If the agent starts reading before showing it, stop it, steer narrower, say *"continue"*.
beats.got: Too much text. I think: ask for plan first, say continue.

beats.trigger: Push back, sharpen, add what's missing.
beats.got: It listed what it could look for. It did not know our depots, so I told it. It listed my weekly delivery report as a source.

beats.trigger: The agent pulls in the content for `sources/`. You don't copy-paste.
beats.got: It took the files I pointed to. Some things were NOT REACHABLE, our system, as expected. I gave it two Excel exports by hand.

beats.trigger: Read the plan before saying go.
beats.got: The plan was short, 6 pages. I merged two. Then it wrote them. I could read it, it was about my work.

beats.trigger: That list is your first quality check.
beats.got: It showed what it is unsure about. Vantaa was missing. Useful, like a checklist.

beats.trigger: Citations show whether the agent read the memory or the LLM filled in from training data.
beats.got: I asked it a real question about the pilot load and it named my files in the answer. So it is not making things up.

beats.trigger: Push back if a claim "got sharper" but the top didn't change.
beats.got: I added one more report and the page got shorter and better. The first answer was less wrong after.

beats.trigger: Reject the ones that miss; the agent applies the ones you approve.
beats.got: It proposed cleanups. I said no to two, yes to the rest. Fast.

beats.trigger: If the answer is specific and every claim has a citation, the memory works.
beats.got: I asked where dispatch breaks if the pilot doubles the calls. It gave a specific answer with sources. I could take this to my depot managers.

beats.trigger: A memory is *files you keep*, not a thread you close.
beats.got: Files stay, chat goes away. Okay.

beats.trigger: three topic pages *got sharper instead of longer*
beats.got: This I saw myself, so I believe it.

beats.trigger: An agent with no files is a chat.
beats.got: Files plus instructions is a system. I got that from doing it.

beats.trigger: The existing memory was part of the prompt for updating the memory
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Keep the rules small and boring.
beats.got: Short rules. Fine, I like boring.

beats.trigger: No database, special tool or paid tier is needed.
beats.got: It is just text files. So no IT project needed for this part.

beats.trigger: Sharpen the memory, never the sources, or you lose the evidence.
beats.got: Do not edit the original reports. Makes sense.

beats.trigger: *Generic AI becomes your AI when you build the memory it reads.*
beats.got: Nice line but I knew it from the exercise.

beats.trigger: The agent comes back with three pointed requests.
beats.got: It said one page sounded like any logistics company and asked me for our real rules. I gave it the Sweden border rule.

beats.trigger: Most of what you know about your company sits in heads and corridors, and nobody has written it down.
beats.got: True. Half of how the depots work is in the depot managers' heads. This is why it did not know Vantaa.

beats.trigger: The agent writes the rules file from the session: what worked, what rubbed, what got repeated.
beats.got: It wrote a summary file of our session. Fine.

beats.trigger: What the agent leaves out is often the signal.
beats.got: Read it and say what is wrong. I changed one rule.

beats.trigger: Every miss turns into a line of context that stops the next miss.
beats.got: When it is wrong, fix the instructions so it is not wrong twice. Like a SOP.

beats.trigger: The model will change under this. The memory will not.
beats.got: My files stay even when the AI changes.

beats.trigger: Plain text: models read and write text best.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: **Daily risk scan**: reads memory, flags the assumption most likely wrong or the question open longest

beats.trigger: Give your daily output the look and feel of your company's website (colours, typography, headers, voice).

beats.got: I clicked Run now and the page opened in browser. It works. Scheduling at 7:00 is just a setting.

beats.trigger: What the agent misses today tells you what to sharpen in the memory tomorrow.

take_homes: If I give the AI my own files, it answers about my business and names the file. Without files it guesses.
It can make a page that looks like our company and run every morning by itself, so a report for depot managers is possible.
Fix it when it is wrong by writing the rule down, then it is not wrong again.

monday.move: Take last week's delivery report export and ask Claude to make the depot table with the right depot names, Vantaa included
monday.who: Me, with one depot manager looking
monday.stop_condition: If I need an IT ticket to get the export, I stop and use the file I already have
monday.blocker: The reporting system only exports through IT, and I have no time this week

misconception.why: The agent answered a question about my dispatch load and cited my own files. That was operations, not a customer chatbot. I have still only tried it on my own notes, not on live reporting.

one_line: Too much reading at first, but when I gave it my own files it answered about my depots and made a nice page. Less theory, more doing, and I would send ops people only for that.
